main_text.head: OCTOSTICHON
JOAN. PISCATORIS, Scholæ Herbornensis Moderatoris, ad IOAN. BILSTENIUM.

p.i: Ingenuas (aiunt) didicisse fideliter artes, Emollit mores, nec sinit esse feros. At didicisse sacri divina oracula Verbi, Informat mores ad pietatis opus. Ingenuas igitur cognosce fideliter artes: Sed Verbi inprimis dogmata nosce sacri: Sic simul humanis ornabere moribus, & sic Divina mentem tu pietate coles.

main_text.head: EPIGRAMMA PHILIPPI à THULEN pro Syntagmatis huius commendatione ad Sophiæ Studiosos.

p.i: Sunt equidem multi, vario distincta colore, Stamina, qui vigili composuēre manu. Sunt quoq; praestātes, glomerata volumina magna, Qui Methodo celebri disposuēre, viri. Attamen hos inter pauci (mihi crede) videntur Aetati imberbi consuluisse probè, Sed valdè implicitis Tyrones artibus omnes Pædeuta, dociles instruere suos.

page.notes: The right edge of the scan is cut off: "Scholæ" in the first title line and "magna," and "pro" at the line ends may be incomplete. The "Ergo" line at the lower right is partly cropped; I have read it as "Erga" and treated it as a catchword. Doubtful: "praestātes" (the macron/tilde and the "st" ligature are hard to make out), "Pædeuta" (the æ may be a plain ae or the ligature), "disposuēre" (the long s is rendered as s, which I have written as s). The large initials I and S have been joined to their words. The ornament under the first title and the rule between the two poems are not transcribed. The first line of the octostich is set with an initial I and the Greek-style spacing has been normalised.
